mainTopic: איסור כולל and שבת on יום הכפורים, when גיד הנשה became forbidden, and the מחלוקת about אבר מן החי in non-kosher animals.
overview: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוסי הגלילי really rejects איסור כולל. It challenges this with a ברייתא about doing work by mistake on a day that is both שבת and יום הכפורים. The answer is to swap the names in that ברייתא. רבי יוחנן then rules that liability depends only on a mistake about שבת. אביי explains this by saying שבת is fixed while the court sets יום הכפורים. רבא rejects that, because both days begin at the same moment. He says instead that the ruling was about one year of persecution, when יום הכפורים was kept on שבת, and the scholars from ארץ ישראל confirm his explanation. The גמרא then returns to the משנה. There, the חכמים answer רבי יהודה that the איסור of גיד הנשה was given at סיני and is only written in the story of יעקב to show its reason. Finally, a ברייתא brings a similar מחלוקת about אבר מן החי, and רבי יוחנן says both sides learn it from the same פסוק about blood. How each side reads that פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי הגלילי really reject איסור כולל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in surprise whether רבי יוסי הגלילי truly does not accept איסור כולל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רבי יוסי הגלילי really not accept the idea of איסור כולל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a surprised question about רבי יוסי הגלילי's view. This line sets up the next move, a ברייתא that seems to show the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא assumed that רבי יוסי הגלילי does not accept איסור כולל. That is the rule that a broader prohibition can take effect even where another prohibition already applies. The question signals that a source is about to challenge this assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'inclusive' prohibition: a broader prohibition that takes effect even where another prohibition already exists.
He does not hold of / does not accept.

phrases.english: And רבי יוסי הגלילי
does he not hold of an inclusive prohibition?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions an assumption about רבי יוסי הגלילי's view that was made just before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is it really true that רבי יוסי הגלילי rejects איסור כולל?

steps.title: The ברייתא about שבת and יום הכפורים on the same day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי הגלילי as saying that someone who worked by mistake on a שבת that is also יום הכפורים is liable for each day separately. רבי עקיבא says he is liable only once.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: if שבת and יום הכפורים fall on the same day, and someone did forbidden work by mistake, how do we know he is liable for each one on its own? The פסוק says 'it is a שבת' and 'it is יום הכפורים.' These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי. רבי עקיבא says: he is liable only once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that both prohibitions, שבת and יום הכפורים, apply at once. That seems to contradict the claim that he rejects איסור כולל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this ברייתא, רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the words 'היא' and 'הוא' that each day counts on its own, so he is liable twice. That means two prohibitions can take effect together. This is the opposite of what we thought he holds. רבי עקיבא, by contrast, says he is liable only once.

keyTerms.meaning: He acted by mistake (unwittingly).
Forbidden creative work on שבת or יום טוב.

keyTerms.term: עַל זֶה בְּעַצְמוֹ וְעַל זֶה בְּעַצְמוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: For this one on its own and for that one on its own, meaning two separate liabilities.
The פסוק teaches; introduces the source in the תורה.
He is liable only once.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Shabbat and Yom Kippur,
phrases.notes: This means the two fall on the same day.

phrases.english: he acted unwittingly and did forbidden labor,
from where do we know that he is liable for this one by itself
and for that one by itself?
The verse says: "It is a Shabbat,"
"It is Yom Kippur,"
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
Rabbi Akiva says:
He is liable only once.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the surprised question of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבי יוסי הגלילי does not accept איסור כולל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, רבי יוסי הגלילי makes a person liable separately for שבת and for יום הכפורים. So two prohibitions take effect at the same time, which goes against the claim that he rejects איסור כולל.

steps.title: Swap the names in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבין sent a message in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: the opinions in the ברייתא are correct, but the names must be reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין sent a message in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: this is the right setup of the teaching, but switch the names.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reversing who said what in the ברייתא. Now רבי יוסי הגלילי is the one who says he is liable only once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions in the ברייתא stay the same. Only the names change places. רבי עקיבא now says 'liable for each one separately,' and רבי יוסי הגלילי says 'liable only once.' That fits the idea that רבי יוסי הגלילי does not let a second prohibition take effect, so the challenge is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: The arrangement or layout of the teaching: the opinions as they are stated.
Reverse; switch the names.

steps.confusionAlert: Nothing in the content of the ברייתא changes, only which name goes with which opinion. After the swap, רבי יוסי הגלילי holds 'only one חיוב.'

phrases.english: Ravin sent
in the name of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina:
This is the layout of the teaching, but reverse it.
phrases.notes: 'משנה' here means the ברייתא we just learned. The opinions stay put; only the names switch.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח רָבִין מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by changing who said which opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversal of attributions in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא has רבי יוסי הגלילי saying the person is liable twice.
steps.terutzMaskana: The names are switched: רבי יוסי הגלילי says he is liable only once, which fits his rejecting איסור כולל.
steps.whatToRemember: After the swap, רבי יוסי הגלילי says that for working on a שבת that is also יום הכפורים, a person is liable only once.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: only the mistake about שבת matters
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the swapped view of רבי יוסי הגלילי. If he was mistaken about שבת but acted on purpose about יום הכפורים, he is liable. If he acted on purpose about שבת but was mistaken about יום הכפורים, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר יעקב בר גיורי sent a message in the name of רבי יוחנן: according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, in the version where we switched the names, if he was mistaken about שבת but acted on purpose about יום הכפורים, he is liable. If he acted on purpose about שבת but was mistaken about יום הכפורים, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical ruling that follows from the corrected version of רבי יוסי הגלילי's view. It shows which day his liability depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the two cases, only his state of mind about שבת decides the outcome. When he was mistaken about שבת, he is liable even though he sinned on purpose about יום הכפורים. When he was mistaken only about יום הכפורים, he is exempt. This shows that in רבי יוסי הגלילי's view, only the שבת prohibition counts here, and the יום הכפורים prohibition does not add on top of it.

keyTerms.meaning: He acted on purpose (intentionally).
According to the version we reversed.
Exempt.

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the swapped attribution into a clear practical result and raises the question the next steps tackle: why should שבת, and not יום הכפורים, decide the liability?
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's ruling: mistaken about שבת means liable, and mistaken only about יום הכפורים means exempt. Steps 5-9 discuss why. רבא explains in step 8, and step 9 confirms, that this was said about one special year.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יַעֲקֹב בַּר גִּיּוֹרֵי
phrases.english: Rav Yitzḥak bar Ya'akov bar Giyorei sent
in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, לְמַאי דַּאֲפַכַן,
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, as we reversed it,

phrases.aramaic: שָׁגַג בְּשַׁבָּת וְהֵזִיד בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: if he was unwitting about Shabbat but intentional about Yom Kippur, he is liable,
phrases.notes: He means liable to bring a חטאת, the offering for a sin done by mistake.

phrases.aramaic: הֵזִיד בְּשַׁבָּת וְשָׁגַג בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: if he was intentional about Shabbat but unwitting about Yom Kippur, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יַעֲקֹב בַּר גִּיּוֹרֵי מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the reversed ברייתא from step 3 and draws out its practical result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי (after the swap): mistaken about שבת and on purpose about יום הכפורים means liable; on purpose about שבת and mistaken about יום הכפורים means exempt.

steps.title: What is the reason for רבי יוחנן's ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן makes liability depend on a mistake about שבת and not about יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the logic behind רבי יוחנן's ruling from the previous step. This short question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said a mistake about שבת makes a person liable, but a mistake only about יום הכפורים does not. Both days forbid work, so why should שבת count and יום הכפורים not? The גמרא wants the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? The standard way the גמרא asks for the logic behind a ruling

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why did רבי יוחנן in the last step count only the mistake about שבת?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's explanation in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why only a mistake about שבת creates liability when שבת and יום הכפורים fall on the same day.

steps.title: אביי: שבת is fixed, יום הכפורים is set by the court
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that שבת is permanently fixed, while יום הכפורים depends on the בית דין setting the month. So שבת counts as the main איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: שבת is fixed and set permanently. יום הכפורים is something the בית דין sets.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. He says שבת is the 'stronger' איסור because it is fixed on its own, while יום הכפורים depends on the court's calendar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבת always comes every seventh day no matter what. יום הכפורים comes on a date that depends on when the בית דין declared the new month. So שבת is treated as already in place, and the איסור of יום הכפורים does not add on top of it. That is why only a mistake about שבת makes him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixed and permanent; set on its own without any court
The court (בית דין), which declared the new month and so set the dates of the holidays
They set / establish (the date)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Shabbat is fixed and permanent,

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים – בֵּי דִינָא דְּקָא קָבְעִי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: Yom Kippur – it is the court that sets it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שבת is fixed by itself while יום הכפורים depends on the court, so שבת is treated as the איסור already in place.

steps.title: רבא: both days start at the same moment
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that, in the end, שבת and יום הכפורים both begin at the same time, so neither one comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: In the end, both of them come together at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's answer. He says it doesn't matter who 'set' each day, because both begin at the very same moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's idea needs שבת to be in place first so that יום הכפורים cannot add to it. But both days start together at nightfall. Since neither comes first, אביי's reason does not explain why only שבת counts.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end; after all is said
Together with each other, at the same time

phrases.english: Rava said to him:

phrases.aramaic: סוֹף סוֹף, תַּרְוַיְיהוּ בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי קָאָתוּ.
phrases.english: In the end, both of them come together at the same time.

steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that שבת takes priority because it is fixed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both days start at the same moment, so it cannot be said that שבת comes first.

steps.title: רבא: it was a year of persecution
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different explanation. It was a time of persecution, and ארץ ישראל sent word that יום הכפורים that year would be kept on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: There was a persecution, and they sent word from there that יום הכפורים of this year falls on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבא rejected אביי's reason, he offers his own explanation of רבי יוחנן's ruling. He says it was about one special year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During a persecution, the leaders in ארץ ישראל sent a message that יום הכפורים that year would be kept on שבת, not on its proper day. So רבי יוחנן was not giving a general rule about שבת against יום הכפורים. He was speaking about that particular year, where only the mistake about שבת made him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A persecution, a time when the government banned Jewish practice
From there, meaning from ארץ ישראל
Year

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying that שבת always overrides יום הכפורים. He limits רבי יוחנן's ruling to one unusual year when יום הכפורים was moved to שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
There was a persecution,
and they sent word from there
phrases.notes: 'There' is ארץ ישראל, where the calendar was set.

phrases.english: that Yom Kippur of this year
is on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected explanation with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits רבי יוחנן's ruling to a specific historical case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן was giving a general rule that שבת takes priority over יום הכפורים.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן was speaking about one year of persecution, when יום הכפורים was set on שבת.

steps.title: The scholars from ארץ ישראל confirm רבא
steps.stepSummary: When רבין and the others who came down from ארץ ישראל arrived, they explained it the same way as רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too, when רבין came, and all those who came down, they said it like רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבא's explanation. The scholars who came from ארץ ישראל reported it the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer depended on an event in ארץ ישראל. The people who came from there, including רבין, confirmed that this was the true story behind רבי יוחנן's ruling. This settles the question in favor of רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who 'went down' from ארץ ישראל to בבל and brought teachings with them
Like רבא; in agreement with his view

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's ruling about a mistake on שבת versus יום הכפורים was about one year of persecution, as רבא explained, and not אביי's rule that שבת is fixed.

phrases.english: And so too, when Ravin came,
and all those who came down,
phrases.notes: These are scholars who traveled from ארץ ישראל to בבל.

phrases.english: they said it like Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין וְכֹל נָחוֹתֵי אַמְרוּהָ כְּרָבָא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The scholars from ארץ ישראל agree with רבא that the ruling was about a year of persecution.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי יהודה's proof from the sons of יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, where רבי יהודה argues that גיד הנשה was already forbidden to the sons of יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: But wasn't it forbidden to the sons of יעקב, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back and quotes a line from the משנה to begin a new discussion. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה holds that גיד הנשה is forbidden even in a non-kosher animal. His proof: the איסור started with the sons of יעקב, when non-kosher animals were still allowed to them. So the איסור of the גיד applied to those animals too, and it stays that way.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve, which the Torah forbids eating
The sons of יעקב, before מתן תורה
Etc.; the quote from the משנה continues

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
But wasn't it forbidden from the sons of Jacob, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה; the 'etc.' means the rest of רבי יהודה's argument there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וַהֲלֹא מִבְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה argues that גיד הנשה was forbidden from the time of the sons of יעקב, so it applies even to non-kosher animals.

steps.title: The פסוק says 'בני ישראל', not 'בני יעקב'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the חכמים challenging רבי יהודה: the פסוק says 'בני ישראל', and the nation was only called that from סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: They said to רבי יהודה: Does it say 'Therefore the sons of יעקב shall not eat'? It only says 'the sons of ישראל', and they were not called 'the sons of ישראל' until סיני!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where the חכמים attack רבי יהודה's proof. They point to the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said the איסור began with the sons of יעקב. The חכמים answer that the פסוק does not say 'בני יעקב'; it says 'בני ישראל'. That name was only used for the nation from סיני on, so the פסוק is speaking about the time of סיני, not the time of יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it actually say...? A way of questioning the wording of a פסוק
The children of ישראל; the name of the nation from סיני on
Mount סיני, where the Torah was given

phrases.english: It was taught: They said to Rabbi Yehuda:
Is it then stated:
"Therefore the sons of Jacob shall not eat"?
phrases.notes: They are changing the wording of בראשית 32:33 on purpose to show what the פסוק does NOT say.

phrases.english: But it only says "the sons of Israel,"
and they were not called "the sons of Israel" until Sinai!

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וְכִי נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's proof from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that גיד הנשה was forbidden from the time of the sons of יעקב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says 'בני ישראל', a name used only from סיני, so it does not prove the איסור existed earlier.

steps.title: The איסור was given at סיני but written in the story of יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים conclude that the איסור of גיד הנשה was said at סיני, but was written in the story of יעקב so we know why it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was said at סיני, but it was written in its place to let us know for what reason it was forbidden to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים finish their argument. They explain why the איסור appears in the story of יעקב if it was really given later at סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איסור itself started at סיני. It is written in the story of יעקב fighting the angel only to show the reason behind it. So there is no proof that it ever applied to non-kosher animals, and רבי יהודה's argument falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: In its place, meaning in the story where it belongs (יעקב and the angel)
To know; so that one will know
Was forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, the איסור of גיד הנשה began at סיני. It is written in the story of יעקב only to explain its reason, so רבי יהודה's proof from the sons of יעקב does not work.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the חכמים deny that the story of יעקב matters. They say it gives the reason for the איסור, but the איסור itself only began at סיני.

phrases.english: Rather, it was stated at Sinai,
but it was written in its place
phrases.notes: 'Its place' means right after the story of יעקב fighting the angel.

phrases.english: to know for what reason it was forbidden to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the חכמים' challenge in step 11 by explaining why the פסוק is placed in the story of יעקב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: גיד הנשה was forbidden at סיני and written in the story of יעקב only to give its reason. So there is no proof it applies to non-kosher animals.

steps.title: רבא quotes a פסוק that uses 'בני ישראל' before סיני
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the חכמים' claim that the name 'בני ישראל' was only used from סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objects: The פסוק says 'And the בני ישראל carried יעקב their father.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the חכמים' argument from the previous step. He brings a פסוק from long before סיני that already calls יעקב's sons 'בני ישראל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said the name 'בני ישראל' only started at סיני, so the פסוק about גיד הנשה must mean the איסור came at סיני. But in ספר בראשית, when the family goes down to מצרים, the תורה already calls them 'בני ישראל'. So the name was in use before סיני, and the חכמים' proof seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And they carried

phrases.english: Rava raises an objection:
"And the children of Israel carried
phrases.notes: בראשית 46:5. This is when the family goes down to מצרים, long before סיני.

phrases.english: Jacob their father"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the חכמים' claim from steps 11-12 that the name 'בני ישראל' only began at סיני.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' claim that the nation was only called 'בני ישראל' from סיני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק from before סיני already uses the name 'בני ישראל', so the name cannot prove that the איסור came at סיני.

steps.title: That פסוק came after יעקב's name was changed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק comes after יעקב was renamed ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא. The name 'בני ישראל' could be used in that פסוק because יעקב had already been renamed ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer narrows the חכמים' point. Before the incident, the sons could not be called 'בני ישראל', because there was no 'ישראל' yet. So the פסוק about גיד הנשה, which is written at the time of the struggle, still cannot be speaking to 'בני ישראל' at that moment.

keyTerms.meaning: After the incident
The event, meaning יעקב's struggle with the angel

phrases.english: That was after the incident.
phrases.notes: The 'incident' is יעקב's struggle with the angel and the change of his name to ישראל.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Timing distinction: the name was used, but only after יעקב was renamed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the name 'בני ישראל' appears before סיני, it cannot point to סיני.
steps.terutzMaskana: The name only became possible after יעקב was renamed, so at the moment of the struggle the sons were not yet 'בני ישראל'.

steps.title: Then let the prohibition start from that time
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks why גיד הנשה should not be forbidden from the time the name 'בני ישראל' began.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: Then let it become forbidden from that time!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא pushes on the last answer. If the name 'בני ישראל' already existed before סיני, maybe גיד הנשה became forbidden from then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים linked the איסור to the name 'בני ישראל'. The name already existed before סיני. So it seems the איסור should begin from that earlier time. That would not be at סיני, which goes against the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Time, moment
Let it become forbidden

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said
to Rav Ashi:
Then let it be forbidden from that time!
phrases.notes: 'It' means גיד הנשה. 'That time' is when the sons were first called 'בני ישראל'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 14's answer and draws a problem from it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' view that the איסור of גיד הנשה began at סיני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the איסור is tied to the name 'בני ישראל', and the name existed before סיני, the איסור should start then.

steps.title: The תורה was not given piece by piece
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the תורה was given at one time, and that moment had no special reason to start an איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Was the תורה given at many different times? That time was not the time of the incident, and it was not the time of מתן תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers. The תורה was not handed down bit by bit, so there is no reason to say an איסור started at a random moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are only two times that make sense for the איסור to begin. One is the moment of the struggle, as רבי יהודה says. The other is מתן תורה at סיני, as the חכמים say. The moment the family carried יעקב was neither of these, so nothing new became forbidden then.

keyTerms.meaning: Many separate times, bit by bit
The giving of the תורה at סיני
The time of the incident

steps.whatToRemember: An איסור can begin either at the time of the event or at מתן תורה, not at some random moment in between. The חכמים' view stands: גיד הנשה became forbidden at סיני.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Was the Torah then given at many different times?
That time
was not the time of the incident,
and it was not the time of the giving of the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the idea of an איסור starting at a random moment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the name 'בני ישראל' existed, the איסור should begin then.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the time of the incident or מתן תורה could start the איסור. The time they carried יעקב was neither, so the חכמים' view stays.

steps.title: A similar argument about eating a limb from a living animal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר say אבר מן החי applies to all animals and birds. The חכמים say it applies only to kosher ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: The prohibition of אבר מן החי applies to domesticated animals, wild animals and birds, whether non-kosher or kosher. These are the words of רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר. But the חכמים say: It applies only to kosher ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about אבר מן החי, much like they argued about גיד הנשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר say the איסור of אבר מן החי covers every animal and bird, kosher or not. The חכמים limit it to kosher species only. Just as with גיד הנשה, רבי יהודה takes the wider view.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb taken from a living animal, which may not be eaten
Applies (said of a law)
Domesticated animal, wild animal, and bird
Non-kosher species
Kosher species

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A limb from a living animal applies
to domesticated animals, wild animals, and birds,
whether non-kosher or kosher,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Elazar.
But the Sages say:
It applies only to kosher ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי נוֹהֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of when גיד הנשה became forbidden and brings a parallel argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים about אבר מן החי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר: אבר מן החי applies to all species, kosher and non-kosher. חכמים: only to kosher species.

steps.title: Both sides learn from the same verse about blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר, as well as the חכמים, all base their opinions on one פסוק: 'רק חזק לבלתי אכל הדם כי הדם הוא הנפש.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Both of them learned their view from one פסוק: 'Only be strong not to eat the blood, for the blood is the life.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן points to the source of the מחלוקת from the ברייתא in step 17. He says both sides learned from the same פסוק. This is the setup: next the גמרא will show how each side reads it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides do not have different sources. They read one פסוק in two ways. The פסוק talks about blood and about 'the life' (הנפש), and the איסור of אבר מן החי is learned from it. The question is whether this פסוק covers every animal or only kosher ones.

keyTerms.meaning: They learned out (a law) from a פסוק by explaining it
One פסוק, the same verse
Life, the living soul of the animal

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this step already explains the מחלוקת. It only says both sides use the same פסוק. How each side reads it comes on the next amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: A two-sided מחלוקת often comes from the same פסוק read in two ways. Spotting the shared source helps you follow the steps that come next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
And both of them derived from one verse:
phrases.notes: The two sides of the ברייתא from step 17: רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר on one side, the חכמים on the other.

phrases.english: "Only be strong not to eat the blood,
for the blood is the life;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the shared פסוק behind the מחלוקת in the ברייתא of step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sides of the מחלוקת about אבר מן החי learn their view from the one פסוק 'רק חזק לבלתי אכל הדם כי הדם הוא הנפש.'
